advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a recall (expect:finding) calibration case for the fail-open MIRROR form (a confident false-FAIL oracle whose instrument received the wrong input / an unseeable format) plus its fixed-form no-fire pair, since both prompt litmuses and the guide introduce it as detectable.
evidence: reviewers/code-review-tests.md:66-68 litmus enumerates 'received the wrong input' as a fail-open world

passing-code-review.md diff: 'an instrument that produces a confident **failing** result for a reason other than the condition (wrong input, a format the matcher can't see) triggers recovery work against a system that was never broken. If you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence.'

ABSENCE: all four tests-eval pairs (R/FP-failopen-absence-oracle, -rederived, -grep-oracle, -truncated-log) and all five base-eval pairs assert false-PASS-under-non-run shapes; none seeds a confident false-FAIL from wrong instrument input, so this branch of the new prompt language is untested.
advisory.finding: The fail-open MIRROR form the diff introduces as detectable behavior — an instrument that emits a confident FAILING verdict because it received the wrong input / a format it cannot see ('name every world ... the instrument received the wrong input'; guide: 'If you are verifying an absence, verify your instrument can still see a presence') — has no recall (expect:finding) calibration case in either eval spec. The only wrong-format case seeded (R-failopen-colorized-grep-oracle) is a false-PASS shape, so a regression where the prompt fails to flag a confident-false-FAIL / wrong-instrument-input oracle would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an R-/FP- pair (e.g. a test that asserts a matcher FOUND a failure but the matcher runs against a format it can never see — a false-FAIL — paired with a fixed form that first asserts the instrument can observe a known presence).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider a dedicated recall pair for the generic 'invisible best-effort failure' base-reviewer bullet if a concrete distinct failure path exists (non-blocking coverage note).
evidence: reviewers/code-review-base.md:57-58 adds a distinct bullet: 'best-effort verification whose failure is invisible'
ABSENCE: base-eval fail-open corpus (R-failopen-unchecked-returncode, -silent-lookup-miss, -environ-scan-skip, -pgrep-self-match-monitor, -pgrep-waiter) maps to the other three bullets only.
advisory.finding: The base reviewer prompt's fourth fail-open bullet ('best-effort verification whose failure is invisible — the code cannot distinguish "checked and clean" from "check never ran"') has no calibration pair distinct from the returncode / silent-lookup / pgrep instances; the generic invisible-best-effort branch is only indirectly exercised.
